A ctml tree standing in the world: a `CTMLSurface` with no one player behind it. Its middle is at the location it was put at, and with `Facing.FIXED` its front faces the way that location looks, yaw and pitch, rolled by `Settings.roll()`. With `Facing.CAMERA` or `Facing.VERTICAL` it turns to face each viewer instead, on their own client.

A hologram is shared or per player, by `Settings.perPlayer()`. A shared one is one tree everyone sees: one player's click, hover or drag is what everyone sees happen. A per-player one gives every player near it a tree of their own, built by a factory and seen by them alone, so what one of them does stays theirs; the factory is how it can, since one tree cannot be in two places.

Nobody is held still. Where anything in a tree can be clicked, everyone looking at it from within reach gets a cursor of their own, seen by them alone, and their clicks work the way they do in a window, through `CTMLClicks`: focus moves, a control takes the click, otherwise the callback under it hears it, and a draggable box or a scrollbar is picked up by one click, follows that player's look, and is put down by their next. Turning the hotbar while looking at it scrolls the box under their look, and the slot only stays put where something scrolled. hover: and the hover callback follow the nearest player looking at a tree, and active: lights up on a press.

`View.presser()` is whoever clicked a tree last, which is how a callback knows who pressed it. Holograms are not saved: a restart or a reload takes them all away.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.paper.render.CTMLHologram;
```

## Members

### `public record Content(DOMTreeElement tree, DOMContext ctx) {}`

What a per-player hologram builds for each player: their own tree, and the context it is shown with.

### `public record Settings(CTMLSurface.Facing facing, double roll, boolean perPlayer, CTMLWindow.Frame frame)`

How a hologram stands: which way it faces, its roll in degrees about that facing, whether each player gets a tree of their own, and how big it is. Yaw and pitch are the location's.

### `public String id(){ return id; }`

The id it was put down under.

### `public Settings settings(){ return settings; }`

How it stands.

### `public boolean isPerPlayer(){ return shared == null; }`

Whether every player near it has a tree of their own.

### `public Location location(){ return location.clone(); }`

Where its middle is, and, when it is fixed, the way its front faces.

### `public boolean isInteractive(){ return interactive; }`

Whether anything in its trees can be clicked.

### `public DOMContext context(){ return shared == null ? null : shared.ctx; }`

The context of a shared hologram's tree, or null for a per-player one, which has one a player.

### `public List<View> views()`

Every tree it is showing now: the one of a shared hologram, or one per player near a per-player one.

### `public List<DOMContext> contexts()`

Every tree's context, for something that wants to reach into all of them at once.

### `public Player presser()`

Whoever clicked it last, in any of its trees, or null where nobody has or they have left.

### `public final class View`

One tree of a hologram, and everything about it that is about who is using it: its surface, its context, hover and press, a cursor for each player looking at it, what each of them is carrying, and who clicked it last. A shared hologram has one, seen by everyone; a per-player one has one a player.
